Sénégal passed a law in March 2026 (Law No. 2026-08) that increased the penalty for "consensual same-sex intimacy" to 5 to 10 years in prison, and it also made public advocacy for homosexuality a crime. Homosexuals were already facing arrests, family rejection, harassment, assault and mob violence, so ironically, some say they're actually safer once they're arrested, because then at least the mob can't get at them. And also ironically, LGBTQ+ people are using this prejudice in their favor to get refugee status and live in rich countries. Anyway, I'm not going to praise communal belonging and ignore the people who have to hide who they are to survive it, or leave.

So which is it? Well, in a way, it's both. It's possible for a society to be spiritually alive, generous, funny and super communal, while still becoming cruel to those who break its social categories. Being in community isn't automatically liberating. It all depends on who is allowed to belong without pretending.
